You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository amueller/word_cloud.

Problem Statement:
WordCloud generation fails with "Couldn't find space to draw" error

#### Description

When trying to generate a word cloud, the process fails with a ValueError stating "Couldn't find space to draw. Either the Canvas size is too small or too much of the image is masked out." This happens even with simple text and default settings.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from wordcloud import WordCloud

# Simple example that should work
wc = WordCloud(max_words=50)
wc.generate("hello world python programming")
```

This raises:
```
ValueError: Couldn't find space to draw. Either the Canvas size is too small or too much of the image is masked out.
```

The same error occurs with various configurations:

```python
# With custom dimensions
wc = WordCloud(max_words=50, width=400, height=300)
wc.generate("some text here")

# With frequencies
wc = WordCloud(max_words=50)
words = wc.process_text("hello world python")
wc.generate_from_frequencies(words)

# Even with very small canvas that used to work
wc = WordCloud(max_words=50, width=21, height=21)
wc.generate("small text")
```

All of these now fail with the same error message, even though they should be able to generate word clouds successfully.

entries.content: The root cause was that the entire word-placement loop in `WordCloud.generate_from_frequencies` had been deleted: after computing the font size and the `occupancy` map, the code jumped straight to building `self.layout_` from empty `font_sizes`/`positions` lists, so no word ever got placed and the recursive font-size detection found an empty `layout_`, raising "Couldn't find space to draw". I restored the loop that scales each word's font size by relative frequency, picks an orientation, locates free space via `IntegralOccupancyMap.sample_position` (shrinking the font or flipping orientation on failure), draws the word, records position/orientation/font size/color, and updates the occupancy integral image. All 76 existing tests pass and the issue's reproductions now generate word clouds successfully.
